columns.corporate_profiles.kyb_status: services/trust.ts resyncKycKyb reads it to decide whether a kyb_v1 legal_obligation is satisfied. The column exists on no table in this schema, so the SELECT throws into its catch, rows is empty, and the whole KYB reconciliation loop is a no-op. NOT given a column, because that alone would not help: nothing anywhere writes a KYB decision. /trust/kyb/start upserts entity_name, registration_number and registered_country and sets the obligation to in_review; there is no provider callback and no admin approve/reject that would ever set a status. Completing the KYB decision path is feature work and a product question — which store, which values, who writes them — not a rename.
